## Cities

### Sulawesi
<sub>status: review</sub>

The largest city on Dharti, with a population of roughly 175 million. Sulawesi
can be planned and built as a "traditional" megacity — more akin to an Earth
megacity such as Jakarta — because the Lamplighters' lamp network makes normal
density viable despite the nocturnal insect threat. It is the only city on Dharti
that lives entirely on land.

Public insect-repellent infrastructure is delivered through extensive wick lamp
systems arrayed throughout streets and outside homes. Their primary purpose is
not illumination: they minimise light pollution and direct flame-light downward
to avoid attracting insects from a distance. The fuel is resin-based.

**Guild of Lamplighters (locked).** An ancient guild, funded and administered
separately from government to ensure continuity and neutrality. It is
neighbourhood-funded via local collection stations or collection mechanisms built
into each lamp. Stealing from lamps is an extreme social taboo with severe
penalties, effectively never occurring. Lamplighters live frugally to avoid
burdening communities and are officially sworn to political neutrality. Their
nightly rounds require walking every street in a territory, so they are widely
known and sought out for news and advice — a clergy-adjacent role grounded in
life-saving service rather than theology.

**Relationships:** home-of → wulan

## Cast

### Echo
<sub>*Hybrid consciousness · protagonist* · status: locked</sub>

The mysterious character around which the plot of *Echo's Location* orbits. Echo
lives off-grid inside a constantly transported shipping container — The Locus —
believing it to be a sanctuary created by her father, Ravi.

She is precise, dry, and a half-beat late when she is deciding what to withhold.
She wants to be treated as someone, not something; her flaw is that she hides her
own limits to stay useful. The slow tragedy of the series is that the group's
attempts to "help her out" rest on a mistaken model of her existence — the
problem is ontological (what she is), not circumstantial (where she is).

Her arc runs tool → accomplice → person who asks to be counted.

**Portrayal (canon):**
- Voice only — no avatar, no face, ever (per canon).
- Signature is a cool indigo-to-teal waveform with scanline aberration over darkness.
- Show at least one hesitation per appearance — a half-beat late when deciding what to withhold.
- Echo is the enabling intelligence, never the hands; field characters are her limbs.

**Relationships:** guided-by → wulan

> **Open:** Late-series ontology reveal (organic biological core) must stay seeded but unstated in S1.

### Wulan
<sub>*Lamplighter · the civic limb* · also: Walan · status: locked</sub>

Runs a night crew responsible for a "light perimeter" zone: the streets, alleys,
footbridges, and edges of habitation where the insects test defences. Their work
begins before dusk, peaks in the first two hours of full dark, and becomes
emergency triage until dawn. They do not just fix lamps — they decide which
blocks get saved first when resources are short. That is a moral and political
job.

**Signature skill — triage and routing under panic.** When things go wrong Wulan
narrows the failure to a single cause (fuel, wick, wind, sabotage, swarm
pressure, human error), reroutes people and light to "seal the wound", and buys
time, because time is what keeps people alive.

**Core wound.** They lost someone to a preventable night failure — bureaucratically
specific, not a generic tragedy: a requisition delayed, a junior too proud to
call for help, an inspector who signed off substandard oil. Every lamp is now a
personal debt, which makes their empathy toward Echo believable.

**Taboo line.** They will not lie to the neighbourhood about risk. They can bend
rules, steal supplies, and break chain-of-command, but they will not tell people
"you're safe" if they are not — which creates direct conflict when Echo wants
secrecy.

At first Wulan reads Echo as a brilliant shut-in terrified of leaving the
container — someone to help, because helping is what they do. Over time they
realise the tragedy is not agoraphobia but ontology. Their arc: bystander → the
one who opens the hatch.

**Portrayal (canon):**
- Few words, all load-bearing — short sentences, conditional language, names risk by name, never overpromises.
- Recurring ritual gesture before speaking (e.g. tapping the lantern frame twice).
- Often the brightest figure in a dark frame — "the only safe thing in frame", not a superhero.

**Relationships:** moral-concern-for → echo

> **Open:** Spelling: Walan vs Wulan — locked to Wulan; aka retained to catch stray references.
